The Committee on the Annual Communication of the Executive Coun
cil, makes the following report :
1st. Your Committee offers congratulations on the prosperous condi

2d. Your Committee calls attention to the fact that the practice of in
itiating Sub-Freshmen, is unconstitutional.
3d. Your Committee recommends that each chapter make a
practice

4th. Your Committee feels that the highest praise is due to the Exec

5th. Your committee recommends a
greater fullness of detail in the
stated communications between the chapters and that symbols be used in
all cases rather than writing the names of officers in full. The Committee
thinks that the observation of these suggestions will be a safeguard
against future impositions.
All of which is most respectfully submitted.

THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OP THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL.
To the Forty-sixth Annual Convention of the Psi Upailon Fraternity :
The Executive Council submits the following annual communication ;
I. Condition of the Fraternity.�
The Chapters nearly all seem to
be in a
prosperous condition. The active membership is the largest on
record. A practice of initiating sub-freshmen at Commencement, has ob
tained in some
quarters, but is evidently a violation of the Constitution.
One Chapter has just abandoned the practice, greatly to its credit.
II. Expulsions.�
W. H. Fox and C. E. Manierre of the Chi, were ex
pelled Nov. 15, 1878. They have since joined a rival fraternity.
in. Alumni Associations. �
In addition to those formed last year,
one has recently been organized at Cincinnati. An annual circular-letter
to graduates would do much to keep alive the enthusiasm of retired
members.
IV. The Diamond.�The Council approves its publication and regrets
its discontinuance. Its members have been unable to do anything to
perpetuate the publication, and announcements that they would were
premature.
V. The Catalogue. �
The volume is submitted for approval or disapprovaL Its cost is $3,000 in paper covers. An assessment of $1,700
upon the chapters is proposed, in proportion to their total living member
ship, with the proviso that all copies thus far sold to the members of each
chapter be credited upon the assessment and books furnished for all
assessments made. The plan merely proposes that each chapter be re
quired to raise its proportionate part of the money needed, by the sale of
books.
VI. Supplements.�
An annual or biennial supplement is recommended
in which shall appear names of new members, changes of address, adden
da, &c.
Vll. Symbols. �
The Constitution provides symbols only until 1880.
If the system is continued it needs amending.

[APPENDIX A.]
REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON CATALOGUE.
To the Executive Council of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity :
The Catalogue was put to press in July last, and the first copies were
ready March 27th. The printing bill is $2,588.18, and other expenses
will amount to about $400. Gen. Res. No. 4 of 1876 required the Chap
ters to revise their lists, from which we understand that they were to bear
the expense of proper revision. From the same resolution we understand
that we were to obtain funds to pay the bills, according to the precedent
of 1870, when the Council apportioned the expense and sent packages to

16
the Chapters, cash on delivery. The $1,200 raised on account, in 1877,
has enabled' us to defer this assessment, and we have not sent books ex
cept upon orders received. With the opportunity for the Convention to
legislate further, the voluntary methods will cease. The Committee must
pay these bills at once, and doubts not that the Convention will provide
means. The A, Z, K, 3, II and X have nearly or quite sold their quota of
books. The success of the most energetic Chapters shows conclusively
that the entire edition can be sold at once, if each Chapter makes a reastmable effort. The Committee is satisfied that the long time spent in pre
paring and publishing the book was well spent, and that all will concede
its wisdom.
Respectfully submitted,
H. L. BRIDGMAN.
C. W. SMILEY.
